$comment: THE CROSS-LANGUAGE VOCABULARY CONTRACT. One home for the words this system agrees on.
Finding H1 of the v0.2 review: 'the system's core vocabulary has no single home - it is
hand-copied across the language boundary'. It has since gone wrong twice in ways that reached
users: the runtime alias map is duplicated in Python and JS, and the agent status vocabulary in
the debug skill still taught six states months after `starting` and `misconfigured` shipped,
which meant an agent could read the skill and RESTART a worker that was already booting.
WHY A JSON FILE AND NOT A PYTHON MODULE. The consumers are in three languages. JSON is neutral
ground that a JS test can read without parsing Python.
WHY THE BRIDGE STILL KEEPS ITS OWN COPY. `install.sh` copies only `mcp/stdio/` into
~/.aify-comms, so a file under `service/` is simply ABSENT on the host where the bridge runs.
Making the bridge read this at runtime would break the native-copy install. So the bridge keeps
its literal map and an AGREEMENT TEST fails the suite if it ever diverges from this file - the
repo's standing rule that a duplication finding becomes an agreement test, not a forced refactor.
Python has no such constraint: `service/api_core/vocabulary.py` loads this file and is the ONLY
Python owner. There is no second Python copy to drift.

agentStatuses.$comment: Emitted by service/status_engine.py derive(). Proof-based: no time-decay states, no `idle`, no `stale`.

meanings.available: Managed and cold-startable, no worker. A send auto-starts it.
meanings.starting: A claimed spawn is coming up; no worker YET. Do NOT restart or re-send - a restart kills the boot in flight. Bounded: falls back to `available` past the spawn window.
meanings.misconfigured: Identity exists but can never start. Not send-recoverable; a human must fix the config.

runtimes.$comment: Canonical runtime ids, and every accepted input spelling that normalizes to one.
